### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **105** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`, `os validate (command, 87 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `45662d2a542d700f904e0593e5cc28468c0e5ae8` — the merge of head `8ef0c16897bc975eb49920df22db292c019f9e45` into base `6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 45662d2a542d700f904e0593e5cc28468c0e5ae8 && git checkout 45662d2a542d700f904e0593e5cc28468c0e5ae8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e 8ef0c16897bc975eb49920df22db292c019f9e45 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e && git merge --no-ff 8ef0c16897bc975eb49920df22db292c019f9e45

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a8f4151d53203268a1913dfcde9caf4d547384e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8ef0c16897bc975eb49920df22db292c019f9e45`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (the one `hits` path `reviewFace` reads off the PR's file list — a published-spec path, so the schema face is served at the same tier as the declared narrowing face; this record covers both), packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-object-names.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/namespace-object-names.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata-audit.object.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-audit-entry.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-host.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.namespace-object-name-doors.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-namespace-object-name.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/package-door-namespace-object-name.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-namespace-object-name.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/spec/src/kernel/namespace-prefix.ts (P's predicate, the one every door calls), packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts and engine-package-registration.ts (the boot path: installPackage runs before registerObject; nested plugins ride the parent's install), packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts (collectPackageMembers, the membership the runtime door mirrors), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts and protocol-package-commits.ts (every authored install, duplicate and upgrade reaches SchemaRegistry.installPackage), packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts (resolveArtifactPackageOrder returns the manifest bodies the CLI walk reads), docs/adr/0150-behavioural-metadata-addressed-by-package-objects-keep-the-literal-prefix.md on main (D6, row K). Not reviewed: .changeset/31681-namespace-object-names.md (prose face, read for ②), scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json (generated ledger, read only).

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged against the tree, not the PR body.

1. `defineStack` (packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, validateNamespacePrefix): refuses a namespace equal to an object name across ONE artifact (top-level manifest + objects, and each `packages[]` entry's `manifest` with its `objects`) and an object `NS_custom`. One call to P's `findNamespaceObjectNameClashes`, riding `StackNamespacePrefixInvalidError` with `issues` = the predicate's sentences; unconditional (not strict-only, line 6405). No schema key, no shape change, no new export — exactly the granted exception. **Right.** The ADR's row K text also names "its declared dependencies' namespaces" for this door; the diff bounds that out because a dependency carries an id and a range (ADR-0141) and never a namespace, and the install door judges it. Guessing a namespace from an id would break red line 2, so the bound is the right reading; see ④ nit 3 for the ADR text.
2. `os validate` step 2c-ter and `os build` step 3a-quater (cli): the same walk over `resolveArtifactPackageOrder(parsed)` bodies plus the stack's own manifest and top-level objects, exit 1, text and `--json` (`errors` rows are the predicate's rows with no wire code, like N's rows). Parity roster lists the helper. **Right.**
3. `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` (objectql): new refusal `NamespaceObjectNameConflictError` (`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, `status`/`httpStatus` 422, `clashes[]`), placed ahead of every mutation beside N's gate. Incoming = manifest namespace + `declaredOwnedObjectNames` of the manifest and each nested `plugins[]` body (computeFQN is identity, so names are compared as shipped); installed = `namespaceRegistry` minus self, `objectContributors` keys minus self-owned and minus the incoming set. Reached by: boot (`registerPackageBody` installs BEFORE registering objects, so either install order sees the other side), `POST /api/v1/packages` both arms, the protocol install primitive, package commits (duplicate, upgrade), the ADR-0146 pair ensure, `sys_packages` rehydrate. Class is module-exported, not package-index-exported, like its siblings `NamespaceConflictError`/`NamespaceNameConflictError`. **Right.**
4. metadata-protocol: new `ProtocolHost`/`AuthoringGateHost` member `objectNamespaceObjectNameClash`; new package export `refuseNamespaceObjectNameClashes` (additive); `PreflightViolationCode` gains `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` with audit spelling `namespace_conflict`; draft verdict rule `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`. Judged at the publish-mode object save (same condition as `NAMESPACE_PREFIX`: object, mode publish, `source` undefined), the per-item publish (on `promoteInto`, sealed managed items excluded), the `publishPackageDrafts` pre-flight (every offending draft named before any promotion) and the draft verdict. An object with no package (environment-authored) is judged against every installed namespace. **Right.** A draft-mode save is admitted by design and told by the verdict; whichever door promotes it refuses — the same disposition the prefix rule has.
5. runtime `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish`: judges every object the metadata service holds under the package before `MetadataManager.publishPackage`, answering 422 `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` through `errorFromThrown`. **Right** (see ④ nit 1 on the re-spelled membership).
6. metadata-core `sys-metadata-audit.object.ts`: doc comment only, the closed pre-flight list gains `namespace_conflict`. **Right.**
7. Nothing widened: no resolver, reader, URL, MCP or SDK path changes; `bare-name-one-holder.ts` untouched. **Right.**

Doors tried and found closed: boot in either order; nested `plugins[]` objects (judged through the parent's install; `plugin.zod.ts` declares no namespace of its own); environment-authored objects; package upgrade/duplicate (through installPackage); namespace change on an installed package (`updatePackageManifest` admits no `namespace`, so only a reinstall can move it, and that is judged; a package re-shipping its old object under a new equal namespace is caught by direction A over its own incoming set); Studio rename (a new save, judged at promotion); `package-duplicate`/`package-unmanaged-import` (write through `saveMetaItem` with `source` undefined, so judged); the stored-metadata migration (`source` set) is exempt exactly as the prefix rule exempts it and defines no new object. Case/fold: the predicate is exact, and both grammars are lowercase-only (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,19}$`, `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`), so no fold can admit what equality refuses.

First-party census (read, not run): 24 distinct `namespace:` strings across examples/**, packages/*/src, templates and fixtures; no first-party object definition, `.object.*` file or object-map key is named like any of them, and no first-party object is named `*_custom`. Matches the changeset's "0 / 0".

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31681-namespace-object-names.md`: minor for spec, objectql, cli, metadata-protocol, metadata-core, runtime; `feat(...)!:` title; BREAKING banner with Why / Before / Now / Who moves / Unchanged and the measured census; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none` with its reason, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. This matches what the diff publishes: an accept-set narrowing at six packages, one additive export (metadata-protocol), one new error class and one new closed-set value, no removed key or export, no stored-shape change. Check Changeset: success. `Clause-②:` line judged right.

Nit (prose face): `@objectstack/metadata-core` ships a doc comment only; `patch` would state it more exactly than `minor`. No effect on the contract.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions` (seat ruled all three "keep"); each judged sound:

1. **Surface beyond the claim — runtime `packages.ts` publish door + metadata-core doc line.** Sound. `MetadataManager` has no manifest and no registry, so it cannot name an installed namespace (its own docblock, and `publishPackage`'s `namespace` option covers only the caller's own namespace); its refusals are `success: false` rows, not a 422. The one caller is the runtime door, which already holds `qlService` and refuses `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` the same way. Dropping it would leave Studio "全部发布" admitting a clashing object with no refusal, against the card's "Studio publish" door. The metadata-core line keeps a documented closed set truthful. Kept rightly.
2. **`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` reused; pre-flight code and `namespace_conflict` audit spelling added.** Sound. The code is already ledgered to metadata-protocol and objectql for "a name the namespace position reads is taken", `check:error-code-provenance` is green on the head, `NAMESPACE_PREFIX` names a different rule, and the install error carries `clashes[]` so a consumer can tell K's clash from the namespace-owner conflict without parsing the sentence. Kept rightly.
3. **`defineStack` clash rides `StackNamespacePrefixInvalidError`.** Sound within the granted exception (a new class would be a new spec export). `issues` are the predicate's sentences and the message names both spellings and both packages, pinned by the test. The header "namespace-prefix validation failed" and the appended hint "Every object.name must be `${manifest.namespace}_${shortName}`" do not describe a K clash — see ④ nit 2.

Dev `deviations`: the runtime door in place of `MetadataManager.publishPackage` (= Q1, sound); the changeset also bumps metadata-core and runtime (right for runtime; metadata-core see ② nit).

Card red lines: (1) resolution never loosens — no resolver or fallback touched; (2) ambiguity reported, never guessed — every clash is listed (`clashes[]`, joined sentences, every offending draft in the pre-flight), and no namespace is guessed from a dependency id; (3) independently releasable — (a) phase-1 one-holder tests untouched, (b) bare-name behaviour unchanged for one-holder names (controls at every door), (c) no migration, (d) declarations present. No narrowing beyond the declared one.

Check-runs on the head at render time: 29 concluded, every one success (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, every Lint family, Type Check source/consumer/debt, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, Live E2E UI, Build Core, Build UI Deps); 0 failed; 13 skipped by design; 25 still in progress (Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Type Check workspace, Type Check UI). The dispatching seat confirms those conclude green before posting; a red one reopens ③.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against ADR-0150 D6 and row K on main: it makes the spec's own refusal real ("a namespace never equals an object name, refused in both directions at every object door, naming both spellings; no object short-named `custom`"). It takes no declared capability away at a consumer: the `NS-NAME` / `OBJECT-ACTION` face and the qualified address are what the clash breaks, and nothing on main promises an object and a namespace on one string. The one predicate is called, never re-spelled, at every door; each door compares against the set it can see and states the set it cannot (the artifact doors never guess the environment; the Studio doors leave the new-namespace direction to the install door that every namespace passes through). No must-fix, no should-fix.

Findings:

- **nit 1 — runtime door re-spells the publish membership.** `packageObjectNames` in packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts copies the `packageId` / `package` / `_packageId` test of `MetadataManager.collectPackageMembers` (private) instead of asking the manager. The two agree today, so the door judges exactly the set `publishPackage` makes live; if the membership rule moves, the door's set drifts silently. Follow-up card: expose the membership from `@objectstack/metadata` (or publish through a hook that judges each member) and have the door read it.
- **nit 2 — `defineStack` header and hint name the prefix rule for a K clash.** `issues` and the lines are the predicate's sentences and the test pins both spellings, so the author is told the right thing; the header and the `${manifest.namespace}_${shortName}` hint are the prefix rule's. Fixing it is packages/spec code (beyond the granted call), so: accepted deviation here, follow-up card to split the header/hint by issue kind.
- **nit 3 — ADR-0150 row K text.** The row says `defineStack`/`os validate` compare with "its declared dependencies' namespaces"; a dependency carries an id and a range, so that set is unreachable at author time and the install door holds it. The tree is right and the seat accepted the bound; the ADR row should be amended (docs prose, outside this PR). Follow-up card.

Nits alone: the round ends here.
